The file is verified. Here's a summary of what was delivered:

---

**`index.html`** — Single self-contained Breakout game with level editor

### Features implemented

| Feature | Details |
|---|---|
| **Level Editor** | Grid of 35×18 cells — click/drag to place bricks (Bresenham interpolation for smooth strokes), right-click or Erase tool to remove, Clear button to wipe grid |
| **Brick Colors** | 18-row color gradient (red → orange → yellow → green → teal → blue → indigo → violet → pink → ... ) |
| **Play Mode** | Click ▶ Play to copy the current grid into an active brick set and start the game |
| **Ball Physics** | Wall bounces, paddle angle-dependent reflection (hit position determines launch angle), brick collision with proper side detection |
| **Score & Lives** | Score display (+10 per brick), lives counter (3 max), bricks remaining indicator |
| **Restart** | Toolbar ↻ Restart button + canvas overlay restart button when won/lost — both re-copy the grid and reset score/lives |
| **Save JSON** | 📋 Preview generates the level data, 💾 Download writes a `breakout-level.json` file via Blob URL |
| **Load JSON** | 📂 Load opens a file picker, validates structure, safely clamps/truncates/pads grid dimensions to fit 35×18 |
| **Keyboard** | ← → / A D for paddle movement, Space/Enter to launch ball, Enter in editor to play |
| **Mouse** | Click/drag draws bricks, mouse-follows paddle in game mode |
| **Touch** | Touch-drag draws in editor, tap launches ball, touch-moves paddle |
| **Win/Loss** | Full-screen overlay with title, final score, and one-click restart |
| **Responsive** | Canvas auto-sizes to viewport, brick dimensions adapt to fit, mobile-friendly CSS |
limitations: No independent browser/visual testing; earlier browser-origin denial honored. VM/DOM/canvas shims do not establish browser compatibility or visual polish.
Single trial per task and configuration; sampling variance prevents strong causal attribution.
